question_text: What is the principle underlying the use of cyanobacteria in agricultural fields for crop improvement?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Nitrogen fixation
lines: Cyanobacteria such as Nostoc and Anabaena
steps.why: Crops cannot use nitrogen gas directly; these cyanobacteria convert it into usable nitrogen compounds, and the heterocyst is the cell where this happens.
common_mistakes: Writing photosynthesis as the principle. The principle here is nitrogen fixation.
Leaving out the word heterocyst — the named cell is usually the marked word.
steps.memory_tip: Two genus names and one cell: Nostoc, Anabaena — heterocyst.
steps.margin_note: The genus names and the word heterocyst are the words to include.

steps.label: Effect on the soil
lines: The fixed nitrogen enriches the soil,

lines.text: N₂ fixed in heterocysts → soil fertility rises.

steps.why: The agricultural value is the end result: fixed nitrogen added to the soil raises fertility, which is why these organisms serve as biofertilisers.
common_mistakes: Stopping at nitrogen fixation without linking it to soil fertility, which is what crop improvement asks about.
steps.memory_tip: Fix nitrogen, enrich soil, improve crop — state the chain in one line.
steps.margin_note: Close with the fertility line — it answers the crop improvement part.

insider_note: This is a cause-to-effect question: name the organisms and the heterocyst, then say the soil becomes more fertile.
